plan.summary:
Webhook payloads now get normalized event names and real HMAC signatures.

- `Event` trims whitespace from the event name.
- `Sign` uses `hmacx.Sum` with the secret. Before, it only hex-encoded the body, so it was not a signature.
plan.riskRationale: Signing is a security-sensitive path. The old code did not use the secret. The new code adds a dependency, `github.com/acme/hmacx`, which was not verified here. Callers and receivers will see different signature values.
plan.storyArc: The change makes webhook output safe to trust. First, the signing fix replaces a plain hex encoding with an HMAC keyed by the secret. Then, event name normalization removes stray whitespace from the payload.

topics.title: Sign webhook bodies with HMAC
topics.narrativeBrief: How does `Sign` change from hex-encoding the body to a keyed HMAC? Check the `hmacx` import and `hmacx.Sum` semantics (hash algorithm, argument order). Note that existing receivers will see different signatures.

topics.title: Trim whitespace from event names
topics.narrativeBrief: What does `Event` return now? It applies `strings.TrimSpace` to the name. Verify that the `strings` import exists, and check whether the callers sign the trimmed value.
